text: These background findings underscore that understanding both the structural and functional modifications of the brain following amputation is essential to comprehend adaptive brain mechanisms and how these changes influence the sensory and motor expressions of affected individuals. In this context, the importance of research exploring the functional connectivity of brain networks through resting-state magnetic resonance imaging is emphasized, providing valuable information on the neurobiological mechanisms linked to sensory and motor adjustments, whether in the short or long term, in individuals with limb amputations.
source_label: Cerebellar functional connectivity alteration in individuals with lower limb amputation
